subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw isolate or preempt compaction and memoryFlush from the foreground session lane, or keep the current foreground-lane model with shorter timeouts and diagnostic recovery?
rationale: The source-backed bug remains, but the durable fix changes scheduler, session-state ordering, transcript rotation, and channel-delivery guarantees rather than one local branch.

options.title: Isolate maintenance lane
options.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated bounded lane or worker so foreground messages can be admitted or acknowledged without waiting for maintenance completion.

options.title: Preempt foreground maintenance
options.body: Keep the current lane model but make compaction and memoryFlush abortable and reschedulable when foreground user messages arrive.

options.title: Accept timeout mitigation
options.body: Treat the 180-second timeout and stuck-session recovery as sufficient, accepting that foreground turns can still block during active maintenance.

recommendation.title: Isolate maintenance lane
recommendation.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated bounded lane or worker so foreground messages can be admitted or acknowledged without waiting for maintenance completion.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent history across reply-run/session-thread and compaction queue surfaces and is the best available routing owner for the cross-cutting scheduler decision.
